name: Youth of Today
label: Revelation
lede: Two kids from a Danbury hardcore band drew a hard line, put an X on it, and taught a whole generation of New York hardcore to wear varsity jackets, skip the beer and the burger, and mean every word.

eras.title: Out of Violent Children
eras.text: Ray Cappo and John Porcelly had already cut their teeth in the Danbury, Connecticut band Violent Children. Youth of Today picked the plainest name it could find and pointed it straight at New York, with a sober, clean-living straight edge message no one had asked for yet.

years.h: Ray Cappo and John Porcelly leave Violent Children for Youth of Today
years.p: Ray Cappo on vocals, John "Porcell" Porcelly on guitar, Graham Phillips on bass, Darren Pesce on drums. Porcell says they picked the generic name Youth of Today so people knew they were there to play hardcore.

years.h: Youth of Today's first show: the Anthrax, Connecticut
years.p: Youth of Today debut at the Anthrax, the Connecticut club that was the region's hardcore clubhouse. John Porcelly credits [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]]'s [[Roger Miret|ab51d57f-5007-4ee4-8461-a4050f8d939d]] and [[Vinnie Stigma|ebc05559-b4e0-4080-87d7-1c6672451491]] with getting them the gig.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ray Cappo · Revelation Records bio · Wikipedia: Revelation Records
years.h: Can't Close My Eyes 7" · Positive Force No. 4
years.p: [[Kevin Seconds|dfa1dec9-a570-4a1c-a2bb-0f07f6dbb81b]] of 7 Seconds releases Youth of Today's first EP on his Reno label, a straight edge stamp of approval before New York knew them. The same year the band appears on the Connecticut Fun compilation LP.
years.xp:
Kevin Seconds was a direct influence on Ray Cappo, and Positive Force was the obvious home: the label had built its name on positive, drug-free hardcore. Graham Phillips and Darren Pesce left soon after Can't Close My Eyes, the first of many exits.

The EP never really went away. Revelation later ran a limited fourth pressing, and in 1997 gave it a full reissue.

eras.title: A crew, a van, a mission
eras.text: The line-up spun like a revolving door, but Break Down the Walls and a 1987 US tour turned Youth of Today into the band every kid in a hooded sweatshirt wanted to be. By the end of 1987 there was a label built partly around them, Revelation Records, and a scene with a name: youth crew.

years.h: Craig Setari and Richie Birkenhead join Youth of Today
years.p: [[Craig Setari|3908d895-a1af-42a7-b86b-93a3074057ee]] comes over from [[Straight Ahead|1fd60d7c-dc35-44f5-9162-4113b6ca4a69]] on bass, and [[Richie Birkenhead|7a1a6273-c31b-4828-8e20-0d6ea66943aa]] joins on second guitar. Youth of Today's drummer keeps changing.

years.h: Youth of Today go through four drummers in a year
years.p: After Darren Pesce, Tommy Carroll, [[Drew Thomas|ebc66701-0d59-49c9-ae21-4937edb96a6a]] of [[Bold|b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa]] and even [[Kevin Seconds|dfa1dec9-a570-4a1c-a2bb-0f07f6dbb81b]] take turns on drums, per Wikipedia. In 1987 Lukey Luke briefly plays bass before Walter Schreifels takes over.

years.h: Break Down the Walls · Wishing Well Records
years.p: Youth of Today's first full-length, cut in two days according to John Porcelly, on the California label run out of the [[Uniform Choice|d514a452-7088-4d49-a03c-9e37d76d38ea]] camp. It becomes the youth crew blueprint: fast, chanted, and aimed at the kids in the room.

years.h: Live at CBGB, June 8, 1986
Revelation Records opens in New Haven
years.p: Jordan Cooper and Ray Cappo start Revelation to release one record, [[Warzone|496da466-68e9-4cbb-9e86-cbb57eda861a]]'s Lower East Side Crew 7". Cappo would step away from the business in 1988.

years.h: New York City Hardcore: Together 7" · Revelation
years.p: Revelation's roll call of the new straight edge New York bands, with Youth of Today leading off.

q: We thought straight edge was an important message.
years.h: Youth of Today tour coast to coast behind Break Down the Walls
years.p: The five-piece: Ray Cappo, John Porcelly, Richie Birkenhead, [[Walter Schreifels|9f350578-acdd-480e-8273-5eaf88842f1c]] on bass and [[Mike Ferraro|edffc714-f0a2-4d6c-b4c0-dc31e713481c]] on drums. Ferraro met Cappo near St. Marks Place and played his first show in Canada with 7 Seconds.
years.xp:
Mike Ferraro learned the set at Giant Studios. The 1987 tour was a rolling argument with the old punk world. In Detroit the locals threw deer meat on stage. In Chandler, Arizona, a Nazi skinhead gang called Youth of Today out to fight behind a McDonald's, then never turned up.

It was also a conversion drive. Buffalo produced its own disciples in Zero Tolerance, and by the band's second trip through Southern California the straight edge kids were packing the room past capacity.

years.h: Richie Birkenhead leaves for [[Underdog|de38fbd3-7155-497a-bf3c-1a8db3091859]]; Sammy Siegler joins
years.p: Richie Birkenhead leaves Youth of Today to focus on Underdog. [[Sammy Siegler|869c662b-574c-46ac-acf6-3dc6f025fd5a]], a teenage drummer out of [[Side By Side|8dc812b1-d387-4c45-8173-f0d5bd0c318f]], replaces Mike Ferraro on drums.

eras.title: India and back
eras.text: The peak year of youth crew was nearly the year Youth of Today disappeared. Ray Cappo walked away, went to India, came back, and the band made We're Not in This Alone, its heaviest, most pointed record: straight edge was the floor now, and vegetarianism was the new line.

years.big: The singer walks out to find God
years.src: Wikipedia: We're Not in This Alone · Wikipedia: Ray Cappo
years.h: Ray Cappo goes to India, and Youth of Today stops
years.p: Youth of Today briefly split while Ray Cappo travels to India, following a growing interest in Krishna consciousness.
years.xp:
Krishna consciousness lined up with everything Youth of Today already preached: no drugs, no drink, no meat. For Ray Cappo it was the next step, not a detour, and it shaped everything he did after the band.

The pause didn't last. Cappo came back to a Youth of Today rebuilt around Walter Schreifels on bass and Sammy Siegler on drums.

years.h: Revelation reissues Break Down the Walls as REV 8
years.p: Revelation, the label Ray Cappo co-founded, reissues Youth of Today's debut LP, and the band appears on Rev's New York City Hardcore: The Way It Is compilation.

years.src: Wikipedia: We're Not in This Alone
years.h: We're Not in This Alone · Caroline Records
years.p: Produced by Ray Cappo and John Porcelly at Chung King House of Metal in New York, the album opens with Cappo announcing Youth of Today is back.
years.xp:
No More is about the meat industry, and its low-budget video cut in slaughterhouse footage from PETA. It's the moment vegetarianism becomes part of the youth crew uniform.

Caroline's original mix of We're Not in This Alone came out muddy. Fans complained, and the label remixed and re-pressed it with a REMIX sticker on the sleeve.

Live Free started life as an unreleased Project X song.

years.h: John Porcelly and Mike Ferraro start [[Judge|3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e]]
years.p: Mike Ferraro, Youth of Today's drummer on the 1987 tour, becomes Judge's singer, with Porcelly writing the riffs. Judge begins as a side project.

eras.title: Out on a farewell
eras.text: Youth of Today took the message across Europe in 1989, including Yugoslavia, which barely had a hardcore circuit, then decided it had said what it had to say. The farewell 7" came out on Revelation, and the members scattered into Shelter, Judge, Gorilla Biscuits and Quicksand.

years.h: Youth of Today play twelve countries on one European tour
years.p: Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Germany, Switzerland, Austria, Yugoslavia, Italy, France, Belgium, the Netherlands and England. A Youth of Today show at Amsterdam's Van Hall later surfaces as a live 7".

q: Straight edge kids were hated back then.
years.src: Wikipedia: Youth of Today · No Echo
years.h: Youth of Today's farewell: the Youth of Today 7" · REV 17
years.p: Youth of Today recorded four songs as a farewell for Revelation, three of which also came out as the Disengage single. Then the band broke up.
years.xp:
Some have read Youth of Today's split as the moment the second wave of straight edge started to fade. The bands that followed took the youth crew sound heavier and stranger.

John Porcelly put it simply years later: the ideals mattered more than the rules.

years.h: Ray Cappo forms [[Shelter|d5157104-76b1-4b8b-90c2-9ff994f940db]]
years.p: Ray Cappo's new band is openly devotional Krishna-core, and John Porcelly eventually joins. Walter Schreifels already has [[Gorilla Biscuits|0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762]] and is headed for [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]].

eras.title: The door never quite shuts
eras.text: Youth of Today never staged one big reunion so much as kept leaving the door open. Short runs of shows, a remixed We're Not in This Alone and a new generation of kids kept the name alive while Ray Cappo's Shelter carried on.

years.h: The We're Not in This Alone line-up reunites
years.p: Ray Cappo, John Porcelly, Walter Schreifels and Sammy Siegler, the Youth of Today line-up on We're Not in This Alone, briefly reunite.

years.h: Youth of Today return with Bold's Tim Brooks on bass
years.p: Ray Cappo, John Porcelly and Sammy Siegler play again as Youth of Today with [[Tim Brooks|f8e01057-29f6-4be5-968e-4220d6a48ff3]] of [[Bold|b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa]] on bass.

years.h: We're Not in This Alone gets a definitive remix
years.p: Ray Cappo and John Porcelly win back the rights in 1996 and make a third, definitive mix of We're Not in This Alone for Revelation's 1997 reissue, with new artwork. Rev reissues Can't Close My Eyes the same year.

years.h: Youth of Today tour Europe with [[Ken Olden|94959ed9-83ae-46e1-b23f-88939fad93e6]] on bass
years.p: Ray Cappo, John Porcelly and Sammy Siegler tour Europe, with Ken Olden of [[Battery|172d89ba-95ab-4e30-92a2-fe836ba0601e]] and [[Better Than a Thousand|9a5d50be-8dff-4f2f-8852-aa4eafb8f985]] filling in. American shows follow in 2004.

eras.title: Back for good
eras.text: The Youth of Today return that started in Lyss, Switzerland in 2010 never ended. The band became a working band again, headlining for kids born long after the CBGB matinees, and by 2016 the 1988 rhythm section of Walter Schreifels and Sammy Siegler was back.

years.h: Youth of Today's comeback opens in Lyss, Switzerland
years.p: Youth of Today start a European tour with Ken Olden on bass and Vinny Panza on drums. By the first week of December they're in Peru, Chile, Argentina and Brazil.

years.h: Youth of Today play Moscow and Oslo
years.p: Youth of Today play two shows in Russia and two in Norway.

years.h: Youth of Today in Washington, D.C., with [[Mouthpiece|e4a55353-84ff-4460-9d5a-1666fbe104f4]] and Give
years.p: Youth of Today play U Street Music Hall in D.C., then the Glasshouse in Pomona and the Chaos in Tejas festival in Austin.

years.h: Youth of Today sell out This Is Hardcore, Philadelphia
years.p: Youth of Today's night at the Philadelphia festival This Is Hardcore is a full house. That October they open for [[Danzig|8925a01a-8608-411d-a90b-f3a52d061208]] at Riot Fest in Chicago.

years.h: Walter Schreifels and Sammy Siegler rejoin Youth of Today
years.p: The 1988 rhythm section returns, playing Berlin that night and Meerhout, Belgium the next.

years.h: Reunion set filmed by hate5six, August 4, 2016
yt: Reunion set filmed by hate5six, August 4, 2016

years.h: Youth of Today at The Book of Revelation Records, Los Angeles
years.p: Youth of Today play night two of Revelation's festival at 1720 with [[Side By Side|8dc812b1-d387-4c45-8173-f0d5bd0c318f]], billed as that band's final reunion show. [[Judge|3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e]] played the night before.

years.h: Youth of Today and [[Bold|b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa]]: four nights in the Northeast
years.p: Pawtucket, The Meadows in Brooklyn, the Lithuanian Music Hall in Philadelphia and Amityville Music Hall, with Swedish Revelation band Speedway on the bills. Thirty-nine years after the two bands first shared a CBGB matinee.
